notes.title: Hints and Tips #1
notes.notes:
Did you know that....

If your troops have been through a particularly tough encounter and are looking a bit battered, they can rest for a turn or two and will recover lost [b]Hit Points[/b] and/or [b]Mana Points[/b] over time.

A unit will recover under the following conditions:
[list]
[*]It did not act in the current turn.
[*]It did not move in the current turn.
[*]It has not received any damage in the current turn.
[*]It does not end the turn next to an enemy unit.
[/list]
The amount the units will recover is calculated using the [b]Recovery Rate[/b] options you can set at the beginning of a Campaign (the default is 25%).

The down-side of troops being idle is that it can make getting the scenario bonus harder to achieve as you are losing time.

Hope the above is useful.

All the Best.

Ian & Jann

notes.title: Version 0.084 Update
notes.notes:
Major update to add new scenario and new features.
[list]
[*] [b]Scenario 5[/b] (Lord Samath) implemented.

[*] [b]New Attributes:[/b] Recovery Rate, Saving Throw Against Magic and Disarm Traps added to all units.

Recovery Rate is a modifier to the [b]Recovery Rates[/b] option that is set in the Campaign Options. It can be altered by spells or by spending character points to improve. For example the spell [b]Restlessness[/b] changes the Recovery Rate by -10%, so if the option set at Campaign Level was that units recover their Hit Points/Mana Points at 25% per turn then the effect of this spell is to reduce the Recovery Rate on the target unit to 15% per turn (25-10).

Saving Throw Against Magic applies to certain spells where the effects of the spell are modified or negated if a unit makes its saving throw.

Disarm Traps would normally apply to [b]Rogues[/b] but can be customized on any unit if required. It represents the percentage chance of a unit successfully removing a trap in an adjacent tile. There is a small chance that an unsuccessful attempt to disarm a trap will trigger it instead!

[*] [b]New Spells:[/b] Stealth (Arcane 1), Levitate, Strength, Weakness (all Arcane 2).

[*] [b]New Foes:[/b] 5 new enemy units added.

[*] [b]New Terrain Type:[/b] Chasm. This makes a total of 31 types of terrain that can influence game play.

[*] [b]AI Spell Casting improved:[/b] The AI will avoid casting spells that may harm its own units.

[*] [b]Sneaking:[/b] Rogues now gain [b]Experience[/b] for each turn they are Sneaking (1% of level range per turn). So for example, a Level 1 Rogue with 0 Experience (requiring 200 points to level up) will gain 2 Experience points for each turn that it sneaks.

notes.title: Version 0.083 Update
notes.notes:
Major update to add new features.
[list]
[*] [b]Story Mode[/b]. Can be selected in the Advanced Rules when starting a new campaign. If turned on, you can select which objectives you wish to tackle when you play a battle (thus increasing the replayability of each scenario).

Note that you can only choose one objective 'thread' for each battle in a campaign but you can, for example, abandon a battle if it is not going to plan and try another objective instead. You could also complete a battle, restore, fight again with different objectives and then move forward to the next battle with whichever Victory 'result' you prefer.

[*] [b]Show Current Unit Dialog[/b] (Options > Interface). Will display a dialog on the left of the screen with extensive details of the unit currently selected. Note that this dialog will not display for enemy units if the [b]Inspect Enemy Units[/b] option is turned off. Active Abilities/Usable Items now share a common dialog on the right of the screen.

[*] [b]Unit Tooltips[/b] (Options > Tooltips). Will display a selectable level of detail as a tooltip when you hover over a unit but can also be turned off. Will not display over enemy units if the [b]Inspect Enemy Units[/b] option is turned off.

[*] [b]Turn Timer[/b]. Can be set for a campaign in the Advanced Rules and limits the time you have to execute your turn. Note that opening any dialog (e.g. the unit profile or the Save Game dialog) will pause the timer. Setting a low time limit can prove quite a challenge if you have a lot of units later in the game!

The Timer is in the [b]Selection Bar[/b] at the top of the screen and will change color as the time counts down.

[*] [b]Floating Text Size[/b] and [b]Floating Text Speed[/b] (Options > Interface). Adjusts the size and/or speed of the text that floats above units. This can be used for example to slow down the text when running at high frame rates or to make the text more readable on lower resolution screens.
[/list]
Game fixes:
[list]

[/list]

notes.title: Design Update: Story Mode
notes.notes:
Hi All.

We're excited to announce that we are currently designing a new gaming feature [b]Story Mode[/b].

At present when you fight a battle there are 'threads' that define the objectives you have to achieve in that battle. The choice of thread is randomized so that you could get a different thread each time you play the battle (although due to the nature of randomization, you can easily get the same thread!) Whichever thread you end up getting, the enemies you face are also randomized so even if you play the same battle/thread in a different campaign, the enemies you face will not be quite the same.

With [b]Story Mode[/b] you will be able to choose which thread you wish to play for a battle which will increase replayability. So for example you could play a campaign and choose Thread A in each battle and then play another campaign and choose Thread B knowing that you will get completely different objectives.

You could also play Thread A in a battle and then play Thread B and decide which one you want to use to progress to the next battle.

At present all battles have 2 threads but the engine is designed to support up to 27 threads per battle. We hope to add more threads if time permits in Early Access, otherwise we will add threads as part of regular updates after Final Release.

We hope to introduce [b]Story Mode[/b] early in the new year. We will keep you posted on progress.

Cheers!
Ian & Jann

notes.title: The Battlefield User Interface (UI)
notes.notes:
Hi Folks.

Today we start a series of posts on the core of the game - the Battlefield. This screen is where you will lead your army throughout the Saga.

Battles will be fought on many different types of terrain. Choose wisely where to position your troops for attack and defense as some will excel on certain tiles whilst others will perform poorly.

There will be one or more objectives that will have to be achieved to win a battle. The objectives may also vary on every Campaign, as will the number and types of enemy you will face. No battle will ever play exactly the same each time. The interface looks like this:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/777cc4967272ff83a1e59d891a3a9e9d0508bddf.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/777cc4967272ff83a1e59d891a3a9e9d0508bddf.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/a94ab4cde28ff450c9c5e427f8f060570c420ddb.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

There are two of your units shown near the top left of the screen. The unit highlighted in [b]green[/b] is the [b]Current Unit[/b] and many of the buttons on the screen will invoke actions or display dialogs for this unit.

Across the top of the screen are displayed:

[b]Undo Button[/b] - Allows the move of the current unit to be cancelled under certain conditions.

[b]Selection Bar[/b] - As you hover the cursor over any tile on the map or you click a specific tile, the Selection Bar will give details about the tile and any unit it contains. The right hand side of the bar also shows the amount of Qaedi you have to spend and the Turn Timer if this has been turned on in the [b]Advanced Rules[/b].

[b]Current Turn Indicator[/b] - Display the current turn number in format 'Turn X' or 'Turn X/Y' if the current battle is turn limited.



On the left and right screen edges you can see:

[b]Active Abilities[/b] - This dialog will show any [b]Abilities[/b] that the current unit can use during its turn. An example might be the [b]Web[/b] ability used by some [b]Spider[/b] units. Using an ability comsumes an [b]Action[/b] for the unit. Most abilities have a limited number of uses in each battle but will recharge between battles.

[b]Usable Items[/b] - This dialog will show any [b]Items[/b] in the current unit's inventory that can be used during its turn. [b]Potions, Scrolls, Consumables[/b] and [b]Tomes[/b] are examples of this type. Using an item comsumes an [b]Action[/b] for the unit. Items are usually one shot and so using it will consume (destroy) the item and it will be removed from the game. Some items however have 'Charges' which will deplete as they are used.



In the bottom left corner are buttons to scale the map (Zoom In and Zoom Out). This can also be done using the [b]Keyboard[/b] (by default the [b]Page Up[/b] and [b]Page Down[/b] keys) or by scrolling the [b]Mouse Wheel[/b].



In the bottom right corner we have:

[b]Next Turn Button[/b] - Will end your turn and activate the AI. You can set options as to whether you want a confirmation dialog to appear and also whether you want to see an animated timer that runs while the AI is playing. This button can be activated via the [b]Keyboard[/b] (default [b]T[/b]).

[b]Screen Menu Button[/b] - Displays a dialog of in-game options (for example [b]Save Game, Player Guides[/b] and [b]Exit Game[/b]). This button can be activated via the [b]Keyboard[/b] (default [b]X[/b]).



Along the bottom edge of the screen are buttons that relate to your units. On the left are the [b]Unit Buttons[/b].

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/f6df0dba6799db51e152aa2dd52f1cb9303ef129.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/f6df0dba6799db51e152aa2dd52f1cb9303ef129.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/fc217bc2977b94805a3f83dc5ee3723b12c55806.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

[b]Purchase[/b] - Not shown on screenshot. This is [b]In Development[/b] and when completed will allow you to spend your Qaedi during battle (for example to buy new units) instead of only [b]Army Management[/b] as at present.

[b]Unit Menu[/b] - Displays a mini-menu that allows quick cycling through your units on screen. The mini-menu allows you to select [b]Previous Unit (with Moves/Actions), Previous Unit, Next Unit[/b] or [b]Next Unit (with Moves/Actions)[/b]. These functions can also be accessed by the [b]Keyboard[/b] by default using the [b]V, B, N, M[/b] keys.

[b]Sneaking[/b] - Only available if the current unit has a [b]Sneaking[/b] attribute of greater than zero (usually [b]Rogues[/b]). Will attempt to sneak which makes the unit invisible to the enemy. If the unit is already sneaking, clicking this button will stop doing so. Available on the [b]Keyboard[/b] using the '[' key by default.

[b]Spellbook[/b] - Only available if the current unit is a [b]Spellcaster[/b] (usually [b]Clerics[/b] and [b]Mages[/b]). Will display the Spellbook page for the current unit. Can be accessed from the [b]Keyboard[/b] using the [b]P[/b] key.

[b]Transfer[/b] - Only active if the current unit is [b]next to[/b] another of your units. Clicking this button will highlight any such units and selecting one of them will display the [b]Transfer Items[/b] dialog. Available on the [b]Keyboard[/b] using the [b]O[/b] key by default.

[b]Inventory[/b] - Displays the [b]Inventory[/b] page for the current unit. Can be accessed on the [b]Keyboard[/b] by pressing the [b]I[/b] key.

[b]Profile[/b] - Displays the profile dialog for the current unit at the [b]Attributes[/b] page. Available on the [b]Keyboard[/b] by pressing the [b]U[/b] key.



Next to the Unit Buttons is the [b]Spellbar[/b]. This is only active if the current unit is a [b]Spellcaster[/b] and allows quick access to selected spells. By default the [b]Keyboard[/b] keys [b]1 to 0[/b] correspond to the buttons left to right.

Ian & Jann

notes.title: Unit Customization (7)
notes.notes:
Hi Folks.

The last 2 buttons on the unit profile are exclusively for [b]Spellcaster[/b] units. Clicking on the [b]Spellbook[/b] button will display a screen like this:

The buttons at the top of the Spellbook will filter by [b]Spell Level[/b]. Beneath a level button is a count of the number of spells the Spellcaster currently knows as well as the total number  of that level they can have in the Spellbook.

Here we can see that the Mage has 2/3 beneath the 1st. Level button and so the Mage currently knows 2 of a maximum 3 spells of Level 1. This is further illustrated by the spells listed on the page with an [b]Empty Spell Slot[/b] displayed for the last spell the Mage can learn at this level.

In this screenshot the buttons for Spell Levels 2-9 are disabled as the Mage does not have enough experience (levels) to learn them.

To find out more information about a spell in the Spellbook, click the '?' icon which in the case of the [b]Flaming Arc[/b] spell will display this screen:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/f8fdb7ac0aa1a2353a214890e809db6a062264c7.png[/img]

Depending on how you have chosen to setup your campaign, you may be able to replace existing spells in a units's Spellbook. The default is that this can only be done before a battle. If the 'Replace' option is available at any time, each spell listed will have the appropriate button.

Clicking the 'Replace' button will display a screen like this:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/6b99bc8282fdbf774946bfe9acb56339c2eef81c.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/6b99bc8282fdbf774946bfe9acb56339c2eef81c.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/89beb9b8a0d20176557c05c071f30f017a48c7b3.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

In this instance we are looking to replace [b]Dodge[/b] with [b]Magic Bolt[/b], so clicking the 'Replace' button beside the Magic Bolt will immediately update the Spellbook for this unit like so:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/2784ad2c5a13189eb8a8af6609730c53d66d4654.png[/img]

It is important to note that each unit has its own Spellbook so you could for example have one unit that specializes in [b]Offensive[/b] spells and another that concentrates on [b]Defensive[/b] spells.

In the [b]New Campaign[/b] setup, you can choose how you want Spellcasters to operate. The default is for Mages and Clerics to have limited spells which is what is shown in this example. If playing with the 'Limited Spells' option, a Spellcaster can use a [b]Scroll[/b] to fill an [b]Empty Spell Slot[/b] (this is covered in the topic on Scrolls).

Happy Casting!
Ian & Jann

notes.title: Unit Customization (6)
notes.notes:
Hi All.

In the previous few posts we've looked at the various stats that define a character's profile. Now it's time to look at the [b]Inventory[/b].

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/4329f7c7058a14e68fe5928b3c412eb901d276f1.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/4329f7c7058a14e68fe5928b3c412eb901d276f1.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/5baac17dc5728bdc995811c483d91e472f8ee27e.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

The Inventory page is made up of 3 sections.

[b]Paper Doll[/b] - a graphical representation of the unit where items are 'equipped'. Any item that is equipped will usually affect one or more stats on the [b]Attributes, Abilities, Movement[/b] or [b]Combat[/b] pages.

[b]Backpack[/b] - where the unit keeps all 'unequipped' items. There is no limit to the number of items in a unit's backpack and they are always displayed in item value order, highest value first. There is also a [b]Filter[/b] field placed just above the Backpack where you can narrow down the items displayed. This is most useful if you have a lot of items in the Backpack.

[b]Action Buttons[/b] - actions that can be performed within the Inventory.

Items are equipped from the Backpack to the Paper Doll by [b]dragging and dropping[/b]. Whenever an item is dragged from the Backpack, the available slots that it can be dropped in are highlighted in [b]green[/b]. Items can be swapped by dropping one on top of another on the Paper Doll. In the picture below the Dagger is being dragged and you can see the right and left hand [b]Melee[/b] weapon slots are highlighted. You can also see that several of the [b]Action Buttons[/b] are highlighted - these are explained below.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/ae439cf8bf363dea14bc1641d92be0f3c8342da8.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/ae439cf8bf363dea14bc1641d92be0f3c8342da8.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/c32bd159e897789458ae15299b802ab27f79f539.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

If the Dagger is dropped on the slot holding the Staff, they will swap places. Also you can see that the Staff is denoted as a 2-handed weapon (with the [b]2H[/b] icon). If the Dagger is dropped on the empty hand slot it will automatically send the Staff into the Backpack as the unit does not have enough hands for the 2 items to be equipped at the same time.

Looking now at the Backpack of this Mage, there is an item in the first slot that is highlighted in [b]red[/b]. This indicates that this item is [b]not usable[/b] by this unit. To reveal more information about an item you can hover over it to reveal a [b]Tooltip[/b] or [b]Right Click[/b] the item to get full details as shown in this screenshot. You can also get full details on an item by dragging and dropping it on the [b]View[/b] action button.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/8e1e89f1a32db7146178aa2e31a3d6d353234bc6.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/8e1e89f1a32db7146178aa2e31a3d6d353234bc6.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/35038f45e292f2ea59e002595c9ac105ad36f786.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

At the top right of the picture you can see that this item is only usable by the [b]Cleric[/b] or [b]Warrior[/b] classes and thus it is [b]not usable[/b] by the Mage.    

The following screenshot shows an inventory for an [b]Archer[/b].

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/72216b992c98f55a40fbb9d353014b019c3c4e31.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/72216b992c98f55a40fbb9d353014b019c3c4e31.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/de7737157637b15a8e8c6e9d73819e3bd67fcf27.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

Compared to the Mage that we saw above, you can see that there are additional slots visible on the Paper Doll. First there is a [b]Quiver[/b] slot (second row down) where the Archer will keep [b]Ammunition[/b] and then there are left and right hand [b]Ranged[/b] slots where the Archer will equip their ranged attack weapon. Archers can have [b]Ranged[/b] and [b]Melee[/b] weapons equipped at the same time. When distant from an enemy only Ranged attacks can be performed but when adjacent to an enemy the Archer can choose to attack with either its Ranged weapon(s) or its Melee weapons(s).

As mentioned above, items can only be equipped in appropriate slots as determined by the [b]Item Type[/b] of the item. The Item Type of each slot is as follows:
 
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/822e12cb69f7d151e71ebc8d5c6c43ed0e1d582d.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/822e12cb69f7d151e71ebc8d5c6c43ed0e1d582d.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/702a1371c8802b4465aabb84a81f577df9db968f.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

Example items:

[b]Melee[/b] - sword, mace, polearm, dagger...
[b]Ranged[/b] - bow, crossbow, sling...
[b]Shoulder[/b] - pauldron, epaulette, rerebrace...
[b]Head[/b] - helm, hat, cap, coif...
[b]Quiver[/b] - arrows, bolts, slingshot...
[b]Necklace[/b] - necklace, amulet, chain...
[b]Cloak[/b] - cloak, cape, shawl...
[b]Bracer[/b] - bracer, vembrace, couter...
[b]Torso[/b] - breastplate, chainmail, mantle...
[b]Belt[/b] - belt, girdle, sash...
[b]Legs[/b] - trousers, pantaloons, cuisses, grieves...
[b]Gloves[/b] - gloves, mitts, gauntlets...
[b]Ring[/b] - ring, band, circlet...
[b]Feet[/b] - boots, shoes, sabatons...
[b]Miscellaneous[/b] - orb, statue, bowl...


Looking now at the [b]Action Buttons[/b], there can be up to 6 displayed depending on where in the game the unit profile is being displayed. The buttons are:

[b]Destroy[/b] - removes the item from the game forever and cannot be undone!

[b]Unequip All[/b] - dragging an item here from the Paper Doll will move all items that are currently equipped  into the Backpack.

[b]Drop[/b] - only available in a [b]Battle[/b]. The item will be placed in a [b]Loot[/b] chest on the battlefield where it can be picked up by another unit.

[b]View[/b] - the same as right-clicking an item, will give a detailed description of the item.

[b]Unequip[/b] - dragging an item here will move that item to the Backpack.

[b]Use[/b] - only available during a [b]Battle[/b] or [b]Army Management[/b]. Using an item will trigger its effects and destroy the item. During a battle [b]Item Types[/b] that can be used are [b]Consumables, Potions, Scrolls[/b] and [b]Tomes[/b]. During Army Management only [b]Scrolls[/b] and [b]Tomes[/b] can be used.

Cheers!
Ian & Jann

notes.title: Unit Customization (5)
notes.notes:
Hi Folks.

It's all about the [b]Combat[/b] modifiers today. Modifiers are split into the following types:

[b]Attack From[/b] - applies to the type of terrain the unit is attacking from.
[b]Defend In[/b] - applies to the type of terrain the unit is defending in.
[b]Protection[/b] - applies to the kind of attack a unit is defending against.
[b]Other[/b] - miscellaneous other stats.

By accessing the 4 combat buttons and using the Loranon Noble elf as an example, the [b]Attack From[/b] page looks like this:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/867e4e8e931678dae8536f5416a169371b1536af.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/867e4e8e931678dae8536f5416a169371b1536af.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/8d5d90106d3bb8080a1dbc55837ec76afdc13fe4.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

You can see from this screenshot that the Elf gets +40% improvement on its [b]Attack Strength[/b] when it attacks from a [b]Forest [/b] tile (the same applies to [b]Wood[/b] tiles which are off the bottom of the screenshot). This is indicated by the 'A' marker in the [b]Buffs[/b] column as the Loranon Noble has the [b]Forester[/b] ability. When attack or defense strength is modified it applies to any [b]Melee[/b] and/or [b]Ranged[/b] attack that the unit has.

So if a unit has a [b]Melee Attack Strength[/b] of 10 with a 40% boost, it has an effective attack strength of 14.

A look at the [b]Defend In[/b] page shows:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/d84214dd2b5ab5f4c92e44eff34994ebccf215fc.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/d84214dd2b5ab5f4c92e44eff34994ebccf215fc.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/b6a50b9d403af6bdad13c3044faad19e8ed2c3a4.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

These stats dictate how well a unit defends in the terrain type it currently occupies. Again you can see the Elf benefits from its [b]Forester[/b] ability.

The third section in combat deals with [b]Protection[/b].

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/82bc56bc61e4abd2a8a57801a66f8b0eea94618a.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/82bc56bc61e4abd2a8a57801a66f8b0eea94618a.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/a217887fb78026a6828a636ef6a3230d1380fdd6.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

Here we can see that the stats are more about what the unit is 'attacked with'. As an example, a [b]Giant Rat[/b] attacks with a [b]Piercing[/b] bite whereas an enemy armed with a [b]Mace[/b] will perform a [b]Bludgeoning[/b] attack. Modifiers on this page can decrease/increase the amount of damage a unit takes when subject to these types of attack.

Finally we have the [b]Other[/b] section. This deals with miscellaneous combat options.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/55b704e2b58d6b67caccf5ba3330e179432342a5.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/55b704e2b58d6b67caccf5ba3330e179432342a5.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/f787ff36f842065d049eb2e7c132b1bd9322b894.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

This shows that a unit can have modifiers when attacking or defending against a [b]Structure[/b] (think Siege Weapons here!)

Cheers!
Ian & Jann

notes.title: Unit Customization (4)
notes.notes:
Hi Folks.

[b]Movement[/b] is the subject of this news item. There are currently 31 different types of terrain that your units may encounter on the battlefield. In addition there are 3 terrain modifiers which are things that can appear in a terrain tile that 'modify' the cost of entering that tile. An example of this would be a tile that contains a [b]Road[/b].

A typical movement page in the unit profile looks like this:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/8f8370177ecb208ea658fcc1e7cc5152ec78e794.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/8f8370177ecb208ea658fcc1e7cc5152ec78e794.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/bdb9c9e0c99b928c23d064e1bdd642eff51b15aa.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

The values shown are how many movement points it costs the unit to enter a specific type of terrain. The [b]Current[/b] values can be modified in-play by spells, abilities and items. The [b]Haste[/b] spell, for example, reduces all movement costs while the [b]Slow[/b] spell does the opposite.

Terrain that this unit is unable to enter is marked with an 'X'. In this shot the Mage cannot enter [b]Lake, Lava[/b] or [b]Ocean[/b] tiles.

The following screenshot shows the lower half of the Movement page.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/e224abfcd0caba680be12ee1c7aa52dcf7a6b588.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/e224abfcd0caba680be12ee1c7aa52dcf7a6b588.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/3f22ba7aeda6eb2b410698c5fafdd50c5f0938a1.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

You can see from the left column that the unit here is an Elf. Elvenfolk operate very well in wooded terrain. This unit has the [b]Forester[/b] ability which gives it improved movement and combat in [b]Forests[/b] and [b]Woods[/b]. This is indicated by the lower movement cost and the 'A' marker in the [b]Buffs[/b] column of the [b]Woods[/b] row (the [b]Forest[/b] row is not visible on this screenshot).

At the bottom of the page are the terrain modifiers mentioned at the start. They are:

[b]Road[/b] - showing that the cost of a tile with a road is -1.
[b]Obstacle[/b] - a whopping +9 to enter.
[b]Snow Covered Ground[/b] - an additional cost of +1.

As most units have 12 [b]Movement Points[/b], examples for the Elf would be:

[b]Plains[/b] - can move 3 tiles (at a cost of 4 each).
[b]Plains with a Road[/b] - can move 4 tiles (at a cost of 3 each).
[b]Plains with an Obstacle[/b] - cannot enter (the cost is 13).
[B]Plains with Snow[/b] - can move 2 tiles (at a cost of 5 each).

Unused Movement Points in a turn are not carried over. Note also that the cost of entering a tile can never be less that [b]3[/b]. So in the case of our Elf, a [b]Road[/b] in a [b]Woods[/b] tile will give no benefit as the cost is already at the minimum.

All the Best.
Ian & Jann

notes.title: Unit Customization (3)
notes.notes:
Hi All.

This one is about a unit's [b]Abilities[/b]. An ability adds a 'perk' to a unit that gives it some in-game capability.

Here is the ability page in the profile of our Mage:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/63938a8868fb8f935a8b11f5aed915179b73ded2.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/63938a8868fb8f935a8b11f5aed915179b73ded2.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/78e10920b268a42d65386865792250ef50749a9f.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

Abilities are either [b]Base[/b] (defines a unit's [b]Class[/b] and [b]Movement[/b]) or [b]Enhanced[/b] (everything else!). So in the case of our Wizard of the Sixth Circle, [b]Arcane Knowledge[/b] makes him a Mage and [b]Walk[/b] dictates how he moves around the battlefield. There is a green icon displayed against the [b]Walk[/b] ability which indicates that it can be upgraded. This will be covered at a later date.

Clicking the '?' icon will provide a full description of the ability, like this:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/5f613a94f0fddee260e0a825b7ee362dac2b12a2.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/5f613a94f0fddee260e0a825b7ee362dac2b12a2.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/9c926e72b985ed46dac64e30999e4023c27bacc0.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

Each ability also falls into one of three types:

[b]Passive[/b] - built-in to the unit and is always 'on'.
[b]Automatic[/b] - is applied whenever a unit attacks.
[b]Active[/b] - is used by choice. Using an ability consumes 1 [b]Action Point[/b].

In the case of an [b]Active[/b] ability, it may have [b]Unlimited[/b] uses or a specific number of uses per battle.

If we take a look at a Southern Worg unit (nasty!), we can see some different abilities:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/c0207941cf32576b4e4ab595caa01a28d9c94097.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/c0207941cf32576b4e4ab595caa01a28d9c94097.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/d5767d96805ada04d96f6bdb54ee7b7238c12a52.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

So this unpleasant creature has [b]Basic Instinct[/b] (which makes it an [b]Animal[/b]), [b]Walk[/b] (so it moves the same as our Mage) and [b]Seeping Wounds[/b]. This last ability is [b]Automatic[/b] and so will be applied to the target each time the Southern Worg successfully attacks.

notes.title: Unit Customization (2)
notes.notes:
Hi All.

The screenshot below shows the 'profile' dialog that you can call up for any of your units (for example during battle by pressing the 'U' shortcut key or the Unit Profile button on the bottom toolbar).

This shot if of a [b]Mage[/b] and it shows 7 buttons along the top edge that give you access to the 7 areas we discussed in the previous post.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/0807f2fd81c32c4479a308d4ff3491345c1dd04f.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/0807f2fd81c32c4479a308d4ff3491345c1dd04f.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/d0e38081a9a23b92f158a4b590ec70ec3d7821ef.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

So today we are highlighting [b]Attributes[/b] which is probably the most important.

The left most column gives you an image of the unit and details of their 'personality' (Image, Name, Type, Class, Species, Race, Size) as well as their current progress in the game (Level, Experience, Equipped Cost). The button at the bottom of this column shows you if this unit has any points to allocate (after levelling up).

The right side of the screen shows base properties for the unit. The column headers are:

[b]Current[/b]  - the value of the stat at this moment in time (the in-play value).
[b]Base[/b]  - the value of the stat without any buffs.
[b]Buffs[/b]  - any buff currently applied.
[b]Range[/b]  - the min/max value a stat can have.
[b]Cost[/b]  - the number of points required to change the Base stat by 1.

The first stat [b]Hit Points[/b] is the most critical. 0 Hit Points = Dead!

Only [b]Spellcasters[/b] will have [b]Mana Points[/b] which deplete as spells are cast. 

Both of these first 2 stats can be 'recovered' by resting the unit during battle. This basically means doing nothing for a turn! They can also be recovered by various spells.

[b]Movement Points[/b] and [b]Action Points[/b] are replenished at the end of each turn.

All moveable units get 12 Movement Points but the cost to enter a tile on the battlefield varies by unit, so plan your moves carefully.

Most units get 1 Action point per turn. Attacking, casting a spell, consuming a potion, using an ability and other miscellaneous activities consume 1 Action Point.

The next section shows stats for [b]Melee[/b] combat. These are the [b]Melee Attack Damage[/b] (how many hit points damage the unit does) and [b]Melee Attack Strength/Defense Strength[/b]. The latter 2 are a measure of how 'good' a unit is at attacking an enemy or defending itself. We will detail the combat mechanics in a later post.

Note that some of the Current values are higher than the Base values. This is because the Mage has an item 'equipped' in the [b]Inventory[/b] which improves these stats (and is indicated by the green 'I' in the buffs column). The type of weapon equipped, it's damage type and whether this is a 'Preferred Weapon' are also shown.

Following this is the [b]Ranged[/b] section. As a Mage does not have a Ranged Attack (that's for [b]Archers[/b]), the only stat shown is how well this unit defends when attacked from afar.

Then we have the [b]Magic Resistance[/b] section. Every spell cast upon the unit is checked against these values to see if the unit 'resisted' the spell. This applies to 'harmful' spells like [b]Magic Bolt[/b] and 'beneficial' spells like [b]Healing[/b].

The last section covers some general but still very important stats.

[b]Spotting Range[/b] dictates how many tiles a unit can see. Principally used when [b]Fog of War[/b] is in effect, any enemy units outside the spotting range of your units will be invisible.

[b]Evasion[/b] gives a unit a percentage chance to avoid [b]Melee or Ranged[/b] attacks. This can also apply to spells cast specifically at the unit if the [b]Directed Spells[/b] rule is in play.

[b]Scouting[/b] governs the unit's ability to 'spot' hidden objects. This could be a [b]Rogue[/b] who is currently [b]Sneaking[/b] around the battlefield and who would be otherwise invisible or it could be a hidden [b]Trap[/b].

[b]Sneaking[/b] (off the page on the screenshot) allows a unit to be invisible to the enemy whilst moving around the battlefield. A Sneaking unit will not be attacked by the enemy and when it attacks it gains a [b]Damage Bonus[/b]. More on Sneaking another time.

Finally another screenshot that shows the different stats available for a unit that has a [b]Ranged[/b] attack (Archers). This shot has been scrolled down so you can see Sneaking stat mentioned above.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/49e02d55f802465194ee6dbc122ebb3bd572b033.png[/img]

Cheers!
Ian & Jann

notes.title: Unit Customization
notes.notes:
Hi Folks.

Hope you had a great weekend. This week we are running a series on how you can customize your units as they level up during the game.

Every unit starts with a host of stats split into 4 areas.

[u][b]Attributes[/b][/u]
This section covers the physical capabilities of the unit (e.g. Hit Points, Mana Points, Melee Attack Strength)

[u][b]Abilities[/b][/u]
Covers the inherent 'perks' of a unit (e.g. Walk, Fly, Forester, Cause Sickness)

[u][b]Movement[/b][/u]
Every unit has the same number of [b]Movement Points[/b] and this section defines how many points are spent to enter tiles of a particular type. There are 25+ ground types in the game from plains, hill and swamp to ocean, sea and stream.

[u][b]Combat[/b][/u]
Shows all the modifiers that apply to a unit when attacking from a tile (based on the type of ground it is on) or defending in a tile (again based on the ground it is on). As an illustration, [b]Elves[/b] are generally pretty cool on [b]Forest or Wood[/b] tiles.

In addition there are modifiers to cover [b]Protection[/b], for example whether the unit has protection from [b]Piercing[/b] or [b]Slashing[/b] attacks (watch out for those Skeletons).

Your [b]Hero[/b] starts with a number of points you can allocate in any of these areas. Each unit gains experience by battling enemies and/or casting spells. Whenever a 'level up' boundary is reached the unit will get a fixed number of 'Character Points' that can be allocated to improve the unit in any way you see fit. The number of points available can be set using the [b]Advanced Options[/b] discussed in an earlier post.


Most units also have:

[u][b]Inventory[/b][/u]
Here is where you equip each unit using a traditional 'rag doll' figure. Units can carry an unlimited number of items in their 'backpack' and can have up to 23 slots where these items can be 'equipped'. Equipped items affect your character's stats, those in the 'backpack' do not.

The slots available on a unit are varied depending on the unit type. For example, the teachings of [b]Children of the Inner Light[/b] devotees require that they cannot wear headgear nor anything on their hands and feet so that they are always fully attuned with their environment. These units do not have [b]Head, Gloves or Feet[/b] slots.

And finally [b]Spellcasters[/b] have :

[u][b]Spellbook[/b][/u]
Every spellcaster has their own spellbook. By default spellcasters are also limited in how many spells of each level they can have in the book at any one time. As a spellcaster levels up they have access to more spells and/or higher level spells. Getting extra spells requires finding or buying scrolls. These can then be copied into any empty spell slot the unit may have (this also destroys the scroll).

[u][b]Spellbar[/b][/u]
During battle the Spellbar appears along the bottom of the screen and gives the currently selected unit access to 10 spells. Others can be cast by calling up the spellbook for the unit. You can customize this bar for each unt to have your favorites readily available for quick casting.

The next post will cover the [b]Attributes[/b] stats in more detail.

Cheers!
Ian & Jann

A unit 'recovers' when it is idle. If the unit does not move or act in a turn [u]and[/u] it ends the turn not adjacent to any enemies, it will regain a percentage of lost [b]Hit Points[/b]. In the case of a [b]Spellcaster[/b] it will also regain spent [b]Mana Points[/b].

The settings you can modify here are all about managing your army between battles. During this part of the game you can have access to 3 areas:

- The Shop (buy and sell inventory items)
- The Temple (buy cures for certain ailments)
- The Training Grounds (buy abilities or experience to improve your troops)

You earn Qaedi (the global currency) by completing battles and looting fallen enemies. You can also sell any equipment you have looted and don't need to raise some extra cash.

Any of these areas can be turned off to change the way you play. So for example, if you turn off the Temple you will only be able to Resurrect fallen troops if your Clerics have the appropriate spell.

Happy Shopping!
Ian & Jann

notes.title: Setting Up a New Campaign (3)
notes.notes:
Hi Folks.

You guessed it, today we will take a quick look at option 3 on the 'New Campaign' menu, 'Spells and Abilities'.

We built these options so you can have more fun with your spellcasters (Mages and Clerics). The idea is that you can make them more or less powerful as you see fit. So for example you can limit the number of spells that a spellcaster has in its spellbook (the same way as D&D and this is the default by the way).

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/a0e637dbf13afbc9d9f47dbf670f124607e3474d.png[/img]

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/a0e637dbf13afbc9d9f47dbf670f124607e3474d.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33719766/804a505beaa1416dbed7a2fcb2e184e9399d158a.png[/img][/url] (Click to download)

Another option is [u]when[/u] you can update the spellbooks for your units. The default is that you take in to battle whatever is currently in the spellbooks and can't change the spells during a fight. So for example if you come across a Giant Tarantula and none of your Clerics is carrying a Cure Poison spell, you could be in a spot of bother!

The other possibilities are that once written into a spellbook a spell can never be changed or alternatively a spell can be changed at any time (even during battle). This last option makes spellcasters very much more powerful as you can nerf a spellcaster to deal with any situation you come across.

New spells are added to a unit's spellbook by finding/buying scrolls and then 'using' them. We will do a video on this another time.

Good Casting!
Ian & Jann
